Responsible Gaming
At Mfortune, we want gambling to remain a form of entertainment, not a source of stress or financial harm. Responsible gaming means making informed choices, setting personal boundaries, and recognising the signs that play may no longer be enjoyable. This page explains the safer gambling approach we encourage, the tools we may offer to help you stay in control, and the steps you can take if you are worried about your own play or the play of someone close to you.
Gambling Should Feel Like Entertainment
A healthy relationship with gambling is based on clear expectations: you play with money you can afford to lose, you accept that outcomes are random, and you treat winnings as a bonus rather than a plan. Problems often start when gambling becomes a way to chase losses, cope with low mood, or escape everyday pressures. Keeping gambling in its place is easier when you treat it like other paid leisure activities and plan your spend ahead of time.
Key Principles For Safer Play
Tools That Can Help You Stay In Control
Depending on how your account is set up and what is available in your jurisdiction, Mfortune may provide features that help you manage play. These tools are most effective when you use them proactively, before gambling feels difficult to control.
Deposit And Spend Limits
Limits help prevent unplanned spending. You can choose a daily, weekly, or monthly deposit cap and stick to it. Limits are intended to support thoughtful play, so increasing a limit may require additional checks or a cooling-off period before the change becomes active.
Session Reminders
Reality checks or session reminders can display information while you play, such as how long you have been logged in or how your session is going. These prompts can help you pause and decide whether you want to continue.
Cooling-Off Periods
A cooling-off period is a short, temporary break from gambling. It can be useful if you notice you are playing more than you planned or if you want time to reset your habits. During a cooling-off period you will not be able to access gambling features, and any attempt to remove the break may not take effect immediately.
Self-Exclusion
Self-exclusion is a longer, more formal way to stop gambling for a chosen period. In Great Britain, multi-operator self-exclusion schemes may be available. If you decide to self-exclude, we encourage you to choose a period that reflects your needs and to treat the exclusion as a protective boundary rather than a challenge to overcome.
Recognising Signs Of Gambling Harm
It is not always obvious when gambling is shifting from entertainment to a problem. Harm can show up as financial pressure, emotional stress, or changes in relationships. You should consider stepping back and seeking support if you notice any of the following patterns.
Support For Players And Families
If you are concerned about your gambling, you do not have to manage it alone. Many people find that speaking to a trained adviser helps them understand their triggers and develop a plan. In the United Kingdom there are specialist organisations that offer free and confidential help for gambling-related harm, including support for affected family members. If you are worried about someone else, focus on support rather than blame: encourage them to take a break, reduce access to money used for gambling, and consider professional advice.
Keeping Accounts Secure And Safer
Account security is part of responsible gaming. Keep your login details private, avoid sharing devices where possible, and do not let anyone gamble using your account. Gambling under someone else’s name can create serious risks, including disputes over deposits, withdrawals, and activity history. If you suspect your account has been accessed by someone else, contact us as soon as possible so we can help you secure it.
Underage Gambling Is Not Allowed
Mfortune is intended for adults only. If you are in the United Kingdom, you must be at least 18 to gamble. We may use age and identity checks to help prevent underage access. If you are a parent or guardian, consider using device-level controls, restricting access to payment methods, and talking openly with young people about the risks of gambling and the difference between gaming-style features and real-money gambling.
Advertising, Fairness, And Player Wellbeing
Safer gambling also means providing information that supports informed decisions. Games and betting products are based on chance or uncertain outcomes. No strategy can guarantee winnings, and short-term results do not predict what will happen next. If you ever feel that you are making decisions impulsively, step away and return later, or use a break tool. Your wellbeing is more important than continuing a session.
Need Help Or Want To Apply Limits?
If you would like help applying a limit, taking a break, or understanding available safer gambling options, contact our support team at info@lymingeprimaryschool.co.uk. If you are in immediate distress or feel at risk of harm, seek urgent help from local emergency services or a trusted professional. Availability of tools and services varies by jurisdiction.
